concepts.name: Measuring length, volume and time
concepts.description: Rulers, measuring cylinders, Vernier callipers and micrometer screw gauges (ZIMSEC), clocks and digital timers; reading scales to the nearest fraction of a division; measuring multiples to find a small distance or a short time, including the period of a pendulum.

concepts.name: SI units, prefixes and derived units
concepts.description: The SI base units, common prefixes (n, µ, m, c, k, M, G) and standard form; derived units such as the newton, joule, watt, pascal, volt and ohm built from base units (ZIMSEC 1.1). Cambridge uses the same units throughout its papers.

concepts.name: Scalars and vectors
concepts.description: Scalars (magnitude only) and vectors (magnitude and direction) with examples; the resultant of two vectors at right angles by calculation or scale drawing, limited to forces and velocities (Cambridge Supplement); resultant of coplanar vectors by graphical methods (ZIMSEC 1.2).

concepts.name: Density and floating
concepts.description: Density as mass per unit volume, rho = m/V; measuring the density of a liquid, a regular solid and an irregular solid by displacement; predicting floating and sinking from density data; whether one liquid floats on another (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Speed, velocity and average speed
concepts.description: Speed as distance per unit time (v = s/t), velocity as speed in a given direction, displacement versus distance, and average speed = total distance / total time; ticker-timer and light-gate methods (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Acceleration
concepts.description: Acceleration as change in velocity per unit time, a = (v - u)/t; deceleration as negative acceleration in calculations (Cambridge Supplement); units m/s^2.

concepts.name: Equations of uniformly accelerated motion
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only: the equations of linear motion for constant acceleration (v = u + at, s = ut + at^2/2, v^2 = u^2 + 2as, s = (u + v)t/2) and their application. Not in Cambridge IGCSE 0625.

concepts.name: Distance–time and speed–time graphs
concepts.description: Sketching, plotting and interpreting distance-time and speed-time graphs: at rest, constant speed, accelerating, decelerating; speed from the gradient of a distance-time graph; distance from the area under a speed-time graph; acceleration from the gradient of a speed-time graph and changing acceleration (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Free fall and terminal velocity
concepts.description: The acceleration of free fall g (about 9.8 m/s^2 near the Earth's surface; ZIMSEC questions may use 10 m/s^2 when the question says so); motion of falling objects with and without air or liquid resistance; terminal velocity (Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC 2.3).

concepts.name: Mass, weight and gravitational field strength
concepts.description: Mass as the quantity of matter; weight as a gravitational force; g = W/m as gravitational field strength (N/kg), equivalent to the acceleration of free fall; comparing masses and weights with a balance; weight as the effect of a gravitational field on a mass (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Forces and changes of shape: Hooke's law
concepts.description: Forces changing size and shape; load-extension graphs and the experiment; Hooke's law and the spring constant k = F/x; the limit of proportionality (Cambridge Supplement); tension and compression (ZIMSEC 3.1).

concepts.name: Resultant force and Newton's laws
concepts.description: Resultant of forces along a straight line; an object stays at rest or at constant velocity unless a resultant force acts; a resultant force changes speed or direction; F = ma with force and acceleration in the same direction (Cambridge Supplement); Newton's three laws and inertia (ZIMSEC 3.2).

concepts.name: Friction and drag
concepts.description: Solid friction opposing motion and producing heating; drag in liquids and air resistance in gases; advantages and disadvantages of friction and ways to reduce it (lubrication, ball bearings, streamlining) (ZIMSEC 3.3).

concepts.name: Motion in a circle
concepts.description: A force perpendicular to the motion keeps an object in a circular path; qualitative effects of changing force, speed, mass and radius (Cambridge Supplement); centripetal force and acceleration described qualitatively (ZIMSEC 3.3).

concepts.name: Moments and the principle of moments
concepts.description: The moment of a force as its turning effect, moment = force x perpendicular distance from the pivot; the principle of moments for one force each side (Core) and several forces (Cambridge Supplement); equilibrium as no resultant force and no resultant moment; the experiment to verify the principle.

concepts.name: Centre of gravity and stability
concepts.description: Centre of gravity (and centre of mass, ZIMSEC); finding the centre of gravity of an irregular plane lamina with a plumb line; how its position affects stability; stable, unstable and neutral equilibrium (ZIMSEC 3.5).

concepts.name: Momentum and impulse
concepts.description: Momentum p = mv; impulse = F x change in time = change in momentum; conservation of momentum in one dimension; resultant force as rate of change of momentum (all Cambridge Supplement). ZIMSEC 3.2 defines momentum and calculates p = mv only: conservation of momentum is not required for ZIMSEC.

concepts.name: Pressure in solids and liquids
concepts.description: Pressure as force per unit area, p = F/A, in everyday examples; pressure beneath a liquid surface increasing with depth and density; the change in pressure with depth, p = rho g h (Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC 3.6).

concepts.name: Atmospheric pressure and its applications
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (3.6): atmospheric pressure and its demonstrations; the mercury barometer and the U-tube manometer; weather and pressure patterns; hydraulic systems, pressure cookers and water reticulation.

concepts.name: Simple machines: levers, pulleys and inclined planes
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (4.1): uses of levers, pulley systems (up to six pulleys) and inclined planes; mechanical advantage = load/effort, velocity ratio = effort distance/load distance, efficiency = MA/VR x 100%; energy losses and ways of improving efficiency (lubrication, lighter parts, ball bearings, smooth surfaces).

concepts.name: Beams
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (5.1): what a beam is; beam cross-sections (T, L, I, Z, O, H, box and cylindrical, solid and hollow); how cross-sectional shape and depth affect strength; compression, tension, shear and buckling; the neutral axis and the distribution of stress in a loaded beam.

concepts.name: Trusses
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (5.2): what a truss is and why triangles make it rigid; advantages of trusses over beams (strength-to-mass ratio, economy); struts (in compression) and ties (in tension); how a roof truss spreads its load.

concepts.name: Joining materials
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (5.3): joining by pins (nails, screws, bolts, rivets, dowels) and by surface contact (glues, soldering, brazing, welding, plastic welding); comparing the strength of joints by contact area and the number and position of pins.

concepts.name: Large structures: bridges and dams
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (5.4): materials for large structures (wood, metal, reinforced concrete, stone) and their compressive and tensile strength, mass and durability; beam, arch, pier and suspension bridges; arches in large structures; earth and concrete dams, straight and arch dam walls (e.g. Kariba).

concepts.name: Energy stores, transfers and conservation
concepts.description: Energy stores (kinetic, gravitational potential, chemical, elastic, nuclear, electrostatic, internal) and transfers by forces, electric currents, heating and waves; conservation of energy with simple flow diagrams (Core) and multi-stage examples with Sankey diagrams (Cambridge Supplement); forms and conversions of energy (ZIMSEC 6.2).

concepts.name: Kinetic and gravitational potential energy
concepts.description: Kinetic energy Ek = mv^2/2 and change in gravitational potential energy = mgh, and energy-conservation calculations such as falling objects and pendulums (Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC 6.2 calculations).

concepts.name: Work done
concepts.description: Mechanical or electrical work done equals the energy transferred; W = Fd = change in energy, with the distance moved in the direction of the force (Cambridge 1.7.2; ZIMSEC 6.1).

concepts.name: Power
concepts.description: Power as work done or energy transferred per unit time, P = W/t = E/t; the watt; ZIMSEC also uses P = Fv (6.3); measuring a person's or a motor's power.

concepts.name: Efficiency
concepts.description: Efficiency of an energy transfer: useful energy (or power) output / total energy (or power) input x 100% (equations are Cambridge Supplement; the idea is Core); wasted energy usually heats the surroundings.

concepts.name: Energy resources and electricity generation
concepts.description: Obtaining useful energy or generating electricity from fossil fuels, biofuels, hydroelectric, wave and tidal power, geothermal, nuclear fission, wind and solar (cells and panels); renewability, availability, reliability, scale and environmental impact; the Sun as the main source; fusion in the Sun and fusion research (Cambridge Supplement); Zimbabwe contexts (Kariba hydro, Hwange thermal, solar).

concepts.name: States of matter
concepts.description: The distinguishing properties of solids, liquids and gases (shape, volume, compressibility, flow) and the names of the changes of state: melting, freezing (solidifying), boiling and evaporating, condensing (Cambridge 2.1.1; ZIMSEC 7.1; sublimation is mentioned by ZIMSEC only).

concepts.name: The kinetic particle model of matter
concepts.description: Arrangement, separation and motion of particles in solids, liquids and gases with particle diagrams; temperature and particle motion; absolute zero; Brownian motion as evidence for moving particles; diffusion (ZIMSEC 7.1); forces and distances between particles and their effect on properties (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Gas pressure, temperature and volume
concepts.description: Gas pressure from particle collisions with a surface; the effect of temperature at constant volume and of volume at constant temperature; the kelvin scale, T = theta + 273; pV = constant (Boyle's law, Cambridge Supplement); ZIMSEC 7.1 also requires Charles's law and the equation of state p1V1/T1 = p2V2/T2.

concepts.name: Thermal expansion
concepts.description: Thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases and the relative order of magnitude, explained by particles (Cambridge Supplement); everyday applications and consequences: gaps in bridges and railway lines, sagging power cables, bimetallic strips and thermostats, liquid-in-glass thermometers.

concepts.name: Measuring temperature: thermometers
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (7.2): physical properties that vary with temperature; fixed points; liquid-in-glass (laboratory and clinical) thermometers and thermocouples; sensitivity, range and linearity; advantages and disadvantages of each type.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity
concepts.description: Internal energy rises with temperature; temperature rise as an increase in the average kinetic energy of the particles; specific heat capacity c = E/(m x temperature change), Q = mc(theta2 - theta1) = IVt with an electric heater; experiments for a solid and a liquid (Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC 7.2).

concepts.name: Melting, boiling and evaporation
concepts.description: Melting and boiling with energy input and no temperature change; melting and boiling points of water; condensation and solidification; evaporation and cooling, factors affecting evaporation, boiling versus evaporation (Cambridge Supplement); the effect of impurities and pressure on melting and boiling points (ZIMSEC 7.2).

concepts.name: Specific latent heat
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (7.2): specific latent heat of fusion and of vaporisation; Q = ml; measuring specific latent heat with an electric heater; explaining latent heat in terms of particles. Not in Cambridge IGCSE 0625 (2026-2028).

concepts.name: Conduction
concepts.description: Good and bad thermal conductors and experiments to compare them; conduction by lattice vibrations and by free electrons in metals; why gases and most liquids conduct badly (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Convection
concepts.description: Convection in liquids and gases explained by density changes; experiments with coloured crystals and smoke; convection currents in kettles, rooms and the atmosphere.

concepts.name: Thermal radiation
concepts.description: Thermal radiation as infrared that needs no medium; effect of surface colour and texture on emission, absorption and reflection; experiments with Leslie's cube; energy balance and constant temperature, the Earth's temperature, rate of emission depending on surface temperature and area (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Applying thermal energy transfer
concepts.description: Everyday uses and consequences of conduction, convection and radiation: cooking pans, room heating, vacuum flasks, solar water heaters and solar cookers, sea and land breezes, car radiators, fires (more than one transfer: Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: The four-stroke engine
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (8.1): the induction (inlet), compression, power and exhaust strokes of a four-stroke engine; the carburettor and choke; ignition by spark plug (petrol) and by compression (diesel); comparing petrol and diesel engines; why engines have several cylinders; efficiency as fuel economy; incomplete combustion and soot.

concepts.name: Fuels: social, economic and environmental effects
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (8.1 social and economic considerations): renewable and non-renewable fuels (wood, charcoal, coal, petroleum, biogas, ethanol); deforestation and pollution from fuels; economic effects; safe handling and storage of fuels.

concepts.name: Wave motion and wave properties
concepts.description: Waves transfer energy without transferring matter; wavefronts, wavelength, frequency, period, amplitude, crest, trough and wave speed; v = f x wavelength and T = 1/f; transverse and longitudinal waves with examples (water waves, electromagnetic waves, seismic S-waves; sound and P-waves).

concepts.name: Reflection, refraction and diffraction of waves
concepts.description: Reflection at a plane surface, refraction from a change of speed (depth in a ripple tank) and diffraction through a gap and at an edge; how wavelength and gap size affect diffraction (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Sound
concepts.description: Sound produced by vibrating sources; longitudinal waves with compressions and rarefactions; the audible range 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz; a medium is needed; speed of sound in air about 330-350 m/s and in solids, liquids and gases; measuring the speed of sound; pitch, loudness and quality related to frequency and amplitude.

concepts.name: Echoes and ultrasound
concepts.description: Echoes as reflected sound and their uses (depth finding, measuring the speed of sound); ultrasound above 20 kHz and its uses in non-destructive testing, medical scanning and sonar, including depth and distance calculations (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: The electromagnetic spectrum
concepts.description: Regions in order of frequency and wavelength; all travel at 3.0 x 10^8 m/s in a vacuum; uses (radio, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays) and harmful effects of excessive exposure. ZIMSEC requires no recall of actual wavelengths or frequencies.

concepts.name: Communication with electromagnetic waves
concepts.description: Cambridge only: satellite communication by microwaves (low-orbit and geostationary satellites); mobile phones, wireless internet, Bluetooth and optical fibres (Supplement); analogue and digital signals and the benefits of digital signalling (Supplement).

concepts.name: Reflection of light
concepts.description: The normal, angles of incidence and reflection; the law of reflection; the image in a plane mirror (same size, same distance behind the mirror, virtual, laterally inverted); constructions and calculations with plane mirrors (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Refraction of light
concepts.description: The normal, angles of incidence and refraction; refraction by glass blocks and liquids; light speeding up or slowing down at a boundary; apparent depth (ZIMSEC); refractive index as a ratio of speeds and n = sin i / sin r (Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC 10.2).

concepts.name: Critical angle and total internal reflection
concepts.description: The critical angle; internal and total internal reflection in experiments and everyday examples (prisms in periscopes and binoculars, mirages); n = 1/sin c and optical fibres in telecommunications and medicine (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Thin lenses
concepts.description: Converging and diverging lenses acting on parallel light; focal length, principal axis and principal focus; ray diagrams for real images (Core) and virtual images (Cambridge Supplement) with a converging lens; describing images; the magnifying glass; correcting long and short sight; measuring focal length (ZIMSEC). ZIMSEC: no images by diverging lenses and no magnification calculations.

concepts.name: Dispersion of light
concepts.description: Dispersion of white light by a glass prism; the seven colours of the visible spectrum in order of frequency and wavelength; monochromatic light (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Electric charge and electrostatics
concepts.description: Positive and negative charges, attraction and repulsion; charging by friction as electron transfer; detecting charge (gold-leaf electroscope); conductors and insulators and the electron model; charging by induction, lightning and lightning conductors (ZIMSEC); the coulomb and electric field patterns (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Primary and secondary cells
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (11.2): primary (dry) cells and secondary (rechargeable) cells such as the lead-acid accumulator; sources of e.m.f. including photovoltaic (solar) cells; cells in series; caring for and safely disposing of batteries.

concepts.name: Electric current
concepts.description: Current as a flow of charge; I = Q/t (Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC 11.3); conduction in metals by free electrons; conventional current versus electron flow; direct and alternating current; using ammeters (analogue and digital) with suitable ranges.

concepts.name: E.m.f. and potential difference
concepts.description: E.m.f. as the work done by a source per unit charge moved round a complete circuit; potential difference as the work done per unit charge through a component; both in volts (1 V = 1 J/C); E = W/Q and V = W/Q (Cambridge Supplement); using voltmeters; e.m.f. of cells in series.

concepts.name: Resistance and Ohm's law
concepts.description: R = V/I; Ohm's law and its limits; measuring resistance with an ammeter and a voltmeter; how length and cross-sectional area affect resistance (proportionality is Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC uses R = rho L/A); current-voltage graphs for a fixed resistor, a filament lamp and a diode.

concepts.name: Electrical power, energy and cost
concepts.description: Circuits transfer energy from a source to components and the surroundings; P = IV and E = IVt; the kilowatt-hour and the cost of electricity from meter readings and tariffs.

concepts.name: Circuit diagrams and components
concepts.description: Drawing and interpreting circuit diagrams with cells, batteries, power supplies, switches, fixed and variable resistors, heaters, thermistors, LDRs, lamps, motors, ammeters, voltmeters, fuses, relays and generators; diodes and LEDs in circuits (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Series and parallel circuits
concepts.description: Current in series and parallel circuits; combined e.m.f. of cells in series; combined resistance in series (R = R1 + R2) and in parallel (smaller than either; 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 is Cambridge Supplement and ZIMSEC); sums of currents at junctions and of p.d.s around a series circuit; why lamps are wired in parallel.

concepts.name: Potential dividers and sensors
concepts.description: The p.d. across a conductor increases with its resistance for a fixed current; the variable potential divider; R1/R2 = V1/V2 (Cambridge Supplement); thermistors and light-dependent resistors as input sensors (ZIMSEC 14.4).

concepts.name: Mains electricity and electrical safety
concepts.description: Uses of electricity in the home; hazards of damaged insulation, overheating cables, damp conditions and overloading; live, neutral and earth wires; switches and fuses in the live wire; choosing fuse ratings; trip switches (circuit breakers); earthing and double insulation; wiring a three-pin plug (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Magnets and magnetic fields
concepts.description: Forces between poles and between magnets and magnetic materials; induced magnetism; soft iron (temporary) and steel (permanent) magnets; magnetic and non-magnetic materials; field lines, their direction and plotting with a compass or iron filings; magnetising and demagnetising (ZIMSEC); field strength shown by line spacing (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Uses of permanent magnets and electromagnets
concepts.description: Uses of temporary and permanent magnets: electromagnets in cranes and scrap yards, electric bells, relays, loudspeakers, motors, generators, magnetic storage, compasses and door catches.

concepts.name: Magnetic effect of a current
concepts.description: Field patterns around a straight wire and a solenoid and their direction (right-hand grip rule); plotting them; how the field changes with the size and direction of the current (Cambridge Supplement); uses in relays, electric bells and loudspeakers.

concepts.name: Force on a current-carrying conductor
concepts.description: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field feels a force; reversing the current or the field reverses it; Fleming's left-hand rule; force on beams of charged particles (Cambridge Supplement); forces between parallel currents (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: The d.c. motor
concepts.description: The turning effect on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field and how to increase it (more turns, more current, stronger field); how a d.c. motor works with a split-ring commutator and brushes (Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC 13.2).

concepts.name: Electromagnetic induction
concepts.description: An e.m.f. is induced when a conductor cuts magnetic field lines or the field linking it changes; the experiment; factors affecting the size of the e.m.f.; Lenz's law (the induced e.m.f. opposes the change) and Fleming's right-hand rule (Cambridge Supplement; ZIMSEC 13.3).

concepts.name: a.c. and d.c. generators
concepts.description: The simple a.c. generator with slip rings and brushes; e.m.f.-time graphs related to the coil's position (Cambridge Supplement); comparing a.c. and d.c. generators and the commutator (ZIMSEC 13.3).

concepts.name: Transformers and power transmission
concepts.description: Structure of a transformer with a soft-iron core; primary, secondary, step-up and step-down; Vp/Vs = Np/Ns; high-voltage transmission and its advantages; how a transformer works and IpVp = IsVs for 100% efficiency; power losses P = I^2 R (Cambridge Supplement); eddy currents and laminated cores (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Thermionic emission and electron beams
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (14.1): electrons emitted from a hot metal filament; accelerating and focusing them into a beam; deflection of an electron beam by electric and magnetic fields; uses in cathode-ray tubes and the CRO.

concepts.name: Diodes and light-emitting diodes
concepts.description: The diode allows current in one direction only (forward and reverse bias), its symbol and its current-voltage graph; light-emitting diodes as indicators; diodes as switches (ZIMSEC 14.2; Cambridge Supplement 4.3.1).

concepts.name: Rectification
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (14.3): converting a.c. to d.c. with diodes; half-wave and full-wave (bridge) rectification and their voltage-time graphs; smoothing with a capacitor.

concepts.name: Electronic components
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (14.4): carbon resistors, colour codes and tolerance; choosing components with suitable power ratings; capacitors as energy stores and in time-delay circuits; reed switches; transducers.

concepts.name: Logic gates
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (14.x, from the scope and sequence chart): NOT, AND, OR, NAND and NOR gates, their symbols and truth tables; simple combinations of gates in control circuits.

concepts.name: Structure of the atom
concepts.description: A positive nucleus with electrons around it; forming positive and negative ions; the alpha-particle scattering experiment as evidence for a small, dense, positive nucleus (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: The nucleus and isotopes
concepts.description: Protons and neutrons; relative charges +1, 0, -1; proton number Z and nucleon number A; nuclide notation; calculating the number of neutrons; isotopes; nuclear charge and mass from Z and A (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Nuclear fission and fusion
concepts.description: Cambridge Supplement: fission as the splitting of a heavy nucleus and fusion as the joining of light nuclei, with nuclide equations and a qualitative account of mass and energy changes; fusion in the Sun.

concepts.name: Background radiation and detection
concepts.description: Background radiation and its sources (radon gas, rocks and buildings, food and drink, cosmic rays); detectors connected to counters; count rates in counts per second or per minute; corrected count rates (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Alpha, beta and gamma radiation
concepts.description: Spontaneous, random emission; the nature, ionising effect and penetrating ability of alpha particles, beta particles and gamma rays; deflection in electric and magnetic fields and why their ionising effects differ (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Radioactive decay
concepts.description: Radioactive decay as a random change in an unstable nucleus; alpha and beta decay change the element; why some isotopes are unstable; the effect of each emission on the nucleus and decay equations in nuclide notation (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Half-life
concepts.description: Half-life as the time for half the nuclei of an isotope to decay; calculations from tables and decay curves, including data where background radiation has not been subtracted (Cambridge Supplement).

concepts.name: Uses of radioactivity and safety
concepts.description: Effects of ionising radiation on living things (cell death, mutations, cancer); safe moving, use and storage of sources; time, distance and shielding; choosing an isotope by its radiation and half-life for smoke alarms, food irradiation, sterilisation, thickness control and tracers (Cambridge Supplement); ZIMSEC 15.2 uses, storage, handling and impact.

concepts.name: The Earth, the Moon and the seasons
concepts.description: Cambridge only: the Earth's tilted rotation and day and night; the year and the seasons; the Moon's monthly orbit and its phases; average orbital speed v = 2 pi r / T (Supplement).

concepts.name: The Solar System
concepts.description: Cambridge only: the Sun, the eight planets in order, minor planets, moons and comets; rocky inner and gaseous outer planets and the accretion model; gravitational field strength at a planet's surface and with distance; light travel times; elliptical orbits, orbital speeds and planetary data (Supplement).

concepts.name: The Sun as a star
concepts.description: Cambridge only: the Sun as a medium-sized star of mostly hydrogen and helium radiating mainly infrared, visible and ultraviolet; stars powered by fusion of hydrogen into helium (Supplement).

concepts.name: Stars and galaxies
concepts.description: Cambridge only: galaxies of billions of stars, the Milky Way, distances measured in light-years (1 light-year = 9.5 x 10^15 m, Supplement); the life cycle of stars from protostar to white dwarf, neutron star or black hole (Supplement).

concepts.name: The expanding Universe
concepts.description: Cambridge only: billions of galaxies; the Milky Way about 100 000 light-years across; redshift as evidence for expansion and the Big Bang; the cosmic microwave background, galaxy speeds and distances, the Hubble constant H0 = v/d and the age of the Universe (Supplement).

concepts.name: Experimental skills and investigations
concepts.description: Planning investigations, identifying independent, dependent and control variables, choosing and using apparatus, taking and recording readings, tables and graphs, gradients and intercepts, errors and precautions, and evaluating methods (Cambridge Papers 5 and 6; ZIMSEC practical work and objectives 4.1-4.3).
